Both \(\text{NO}_2\) and \(\text{SO}_2\) are acidic oxides soluble in water that contribute to acid rain and act as reducing agents.

Evaluation of Distinguishing Feature:
Sulphur dioxide (\(\text{SO}_2\)) is widely used as a food preservative and antimicrobial agent (for example, in dried fruits and wine) to inhibit bacterial growth and enzymatic oxidation. Nitrogen dioxide (\(\text{NO}_2\)) is toxic and corrosive, making it completely unsuitable for food preservation.

Final Conclusion:
Use as a food preservative is a property shown by \(\text{SO}_2\) but not by \(\text{NO}_2\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q56 - Maximum bond angle at nitrogen among nitrogen oxide species

questiontext.text: Maximum bond angle at nitrogen is present in which of the following?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Bond angle depends on the hybridization of the central nitrogen atom and repulsion between electron pairs according to VSEPR theory.

Evaluation of Nitrogen Oxide Species:
1. \(\text{NO}_2^+\): Nitronium ion has \(\text{sp}\) hybridization at nitrogen with zero lone pairs, forming a linear geometry with a bond angle of \(180^\circ\).
2. \(\text{NO}_2\): Has \(\text{sp}^2\) hybridization with one unpaired electron on nitrogen, giving a bent shape with a bond angle of approximately \(134^\circ\).
3. \(\text{NO}_3^-\): Nitrate ion has \(\text{sp}^2\) hybridization with three bonding domains and zero lone pairs, forming a trigonal planar geometry with bond angles of \(120^\circ\).
4. \(\text{NO}_2^-\): Nitrite ion has \(\text{sp}^2\) hybridization with one lone pair, giving a bent shape with a bond angle of approximately \(115^\circ\).

Final Conclusion:
The maximum bond angle at nitrogen occurs in the linear \(\text{NO}_2^+\) ion (\(180^\circ\)).
The species with maximum bond angle is \(\text{NO}_2^+\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q57 - Transition metal cation exhibiting magnetic moment of 2.84 BM

questiontext.text: Magnetic moment \(2.84\text{ BM}\) is given by (At. no. Ni = 28, Ti = 22, Cr = 24, Co = 27)

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Spin-only magnetic moment formula: \(\mu = \sqrt{n(n + 2)}\text{ BM}\), where \(n\) is the number of unpaired d-electrons.

Step-by-Step Calculation:
1. Determine number of unpaired electrons \(n\) for \(\mu = 2.84\text{ BM}\):
\[ \sqrt{n(n + 2)} = 2.84 \implies n(n + 2) \approx 8 \implies n = 2 \]
2. Analyze d-electron configurations of the given transition metal cations:
- \(\text{Ti}^{3+}\) (\(Z = 22\)): \([\text{Ar}] 3\text{d}^1 \implies n = 1\), \(\mu = \sqrt{3} = 1.73\text{ BM}\).
- \(\text{Cr}^{3+}\) (\(Z = 24\)): \([\text{Ar}] 3\text{d}^3 \implies n = 3\), \(\mu = \sqrt{15} = 3.87\text{ BM}\).
- \(\text{Co}^{2+}\) (\(Z = 27\)): \([\text{Ar}] 3\text{d}^7 \implies n = 3\), \(\mu = \sqrt{15} = 3.87\text{ BM}\).
- \(\text{Ni}^{2+}\) (\(Z = 28\)): \([\text{Ar}] 3\text{d}^8 \implies\) electronic distribution has 2 unpaired electrons (\(n = 2\)), \(\mu = \sqrt{2(2 + 2)} = \sqrt{8} \approx 2.83\text{--}2.84\text{ BM}\).

Final Conclusion:
\(\text{Ni}^{2+}\) has 2 unpaired electrons, giving a spin-only magnetic moment of \(2.84\text{ BM}\).
The correct ion is \(\text{Ni}^{2+}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q58 - Cobalt amine complex not producing chloride precipitate with silver nitrate

questiontext.text: Cobalt (III) chloride forms several octahedral complexes with ammonia. Which of the following will not give test for chloride ions with silver nitrate at \(25^{\circ}\text{C}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
In coordination compounds, only ionizable chloride ligands present outside the coordination sphere precipitate as \(\text{AgCl}\) upon reaction with aqueous silver nitrate (\(\text{AgNO}_3\)). Chloride ligands inside the primary coordination sphere do not ionize.

Evaluation of Coordination Formulations:
1. \(\text{CoCl}_3 \cdot 6\text{NH}_3 \implies [\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3\): Gives 3 ionizable \(\text{Cl}^-\) ions.
2. \(\text{CoCl}_3 \cdot 5\text{NH}_3 \implies [\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2\): Gives 2 ionizable \(\text{Cl}^-\) ions.
3. \(\text{CoCl}_3 \cdot 4\text{NH}_3 \implies [\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]\text{Cl}\): Gives 1 ionizable \(\text{Cl}^-\) ion.
4. \(\text{CoCl}_3 \cdot 3\text{NH}_3 \implies [\text{Co}(\text{NH}_3)_3\text{Cl}_3]\): All three chloride ions reside inside the primary coordination sphere. There are no ionizable chloride ions outside the sphere, so it yields no precipitate with \(\text{AgNO}_3\).

Final Conclusion:
\(\text{CoCl}_3 \cdot 3\text{NH}_3\) does not give a test for chloride ions with silver nitrate.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q59 - Spin state and electronic configuration of hexacyanocobaltate complex

questiontext.text: Which of these statements about \([\text{Co}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}\) is true?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
In Crystal Field Theory, cyanido (\(\text{CN}^-\)) is a strong field ligand that causes large crystal field splitting (\(\Delta_o > P\)), inducing electron pairing in the lower energy \(\text{t}_{2\text{g}}\) orbitals.

Evaluation of Complex \([\text{Co}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}\):
1. Oxidation state of cobalt: \(x + 6(-1) = -3 \implies x = +3\).
2. Electronic configuration of \(\text{Co}^{3+}\) (\(Z = 27\)): \([\text{Ar}] 3\text{d}^6\).
3. Since \(\text{CN}^-\) is a strong field ligand, all six 3d electrons pair up in \(\text{t}_{2\text{g}}\) orbitals (\(\text{t}_{2\text{g}}^6 \text{e}_\text{g}^0\)).
4. Unpaired electrons = \(0\), making it a diamagnetic, low-spin complex.

Final Conclusion:
\([\text{Co}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}\) has no unpaired electrons and exists in a low-spin configuration.
The correct statement is that \([\text{Co}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}\) has no unpaired electrons and will be in a low-spin configuration.

answer.text: \([\text{Co}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}\) has no unpaired electrons and will be in a low-spin configuration.
\([\text{Co}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}\) has four unpaired electrons and will be in a low-spin configuration.
\([\text{Co}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}\) has four unpaired electrons and will be in a high-spin configuration.
\([\text{Co}(\text{CN})_6]^{3-}\) has no unpaired electrons and will be in a high-spin configuration.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q60 - Arrhenius graph slope determination for activation energy

questiontext.text: The activation energy of a reaction can be determined from the slope of which of the following graphs?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
The temperature dependence of a chemical reaction rate constant \(k\) is given by the Arrhenius equation:
\[ k = A e^{-E_a / R T} \]

Linear Equation Derivation:
Taking natural logarithms on both sides:
\[ \ln k = \ln A - \frac{E_a}{R} \left(\frac{1}{T}\right) \]
Comparing with the straight-line equation \(y = mx + c\):
- \(y = \ln k\)
- \(x = \frac{1}{T}\)
- \(\text{Slope } m = -\frac{E_a}{R}\)

Final Conclusion:
The slope of the graph of \(\ln k\) versus \(\frac{1}{T}\) yields \(-\frac{E_a}{R}\), allowing determination of activation energy \(E_a\).
The correct graph is \(\ln k\) vs \(\frac{1}{T}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q61 - Thermodynamic parameter not equal to zero for an ideal solution

questiontext.text: Which one is not equal to zero for an ideal solution?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
An ideal solution obeys Raoult's Law over the entire range of concentration.

Thermodynamic Properties of Ideal Solutions:
1. Enthalpy of mixing: \(\Delta H_{\text{mix}} = 0\).
2. Volume change on mixing: \(\Delta V_{\text{mix}} = 0\).
3. Vapor pressure deviation: \(\Delta P = P_{\text{observed}} - P_{\text{Raoult}} = 0\).
4. Entropy of mixing: Mixing of two or more liquids increases molecular disorder, making \(\Delta S_{\text{mix}} > 0\) (always positive and non-zero).

Final Conclusion:
For an ideal solution, \(\Delta S_{\text{mix}}\) is greater than zero and not equal to zero.
The correct parameter is \(\Delta S_{\text{mix}}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q62 - Molar ratio of hydrogen and oxygen gas mixture

questiontext.text: A mixture of gases contains \(\mathrm{H}_{2}\) and \(\mathrm{O}_{2}\) gases in the ratio of \(1:4\) (w/w). What is the molar ratio of the two gases in the mixture?

generalfeedback.text:
Given Data and Conditions:
Mass ratio of \(\mathrm{H}_2\) to \(\mathrm{O}_2\): \(w_{\mathrm{H}_2} : w_{\mathrm{O}_2} = 1 : 4\).
Molar mass of \(\mathrm{H}_2 = 2\text{ g/mol}\).
Molar mass of \(\mathrm{O}_2 = 32\text{ g/mol}\).

Assumptions and Sign Conventions:
Ideal gas behavior where number of moles \(n = \frac{w}{M}\).

Relevant Formulae and Principles:
Molar ratio: \(\frac{n_{\mathrm{H}_2}}{n_{\mathrm{O}_2}} = \frac{w_{\mathrm{H}_2} / M_{\mathrm{H}_2}}{w_{\mathrm{O}_2} / M_{\mathrm{O}_2}}\).

Step-by-Step Working:
Let \(w_{\mathrm{H}_2} = x\text{ g}\), then \(w_{\mathrm{O}_2} = 4x\text{ g}\).
1. Calculate moles of \(\mathrm{H}_2\):
\[ n_{\mathrm{H}_2} = \frac{x}{2} \]
2. Calculate moles of \(\mathrm{O}_2\):
\[ n_{\mathrm{O}_2} = \frac{4x}{32} = \frac{x}{8} \]
3. Calculate molar ratio:
\[ \frac{n_{\mathrm{H}_2}}{n_{\mathrm{O}_2}} = \frac{x / 2}{x / 8} = \frac{8}{2} = \frac{4}{1} \]

Check and Final Answer:
Since hydrogen is 16 times lighter than oxygen per mole, a 1:4 mass ratio converts to a 4:1 molar ratio.
The molar ratio of \(\mathrm{H}_2\) to \(\mathrm{O}_2\) in the mixture is \(4:1\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q63 - Atomic radius of metal crystallising in cubic unit cell

questiontext.text: A given metal crystallises out with a cubic structure having edge length of \(361~\mathrm{pm}\). If there are four metal atoms in one unit cell, what is the radius of one atom?

generalfeedback.text:
Given Data and Conditions:
Unit cell edge length \(a = 361\text{ pm}\).
Number of atoms per unit cell \(Z = 4\).

Assumptions and Sign Conventions:
Since \(Z = 4\), the unit cell is face-centered cubic (FCC).

Relevant Formulae and Principles:
In an FCC unit cell, atoms touch along the face diagonal:
\[ 4 r = \sqrt{2} a \implies r = \frac{\sqrt{2} a}{4} = \frac{a}{2 \sqrt{2}} \]

Step-by-Step Working:
Substitute \(a = 361\text{ pm}\):
\[ r = \frac{1.414 \times 361\text{ pm}}{4} = \frac{510.454}{4} \approx 127.6\text{ pm} \approx 127\text{ pm} \]

Check and Final Answer:
Checking relationship: \(4 \times 127.6 = 510.4 \approx \sqrt{2} \times 361 = 510.5\), confirming accuracy.
The radius of one atom is \(127\text{ pm}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q64 - Order of reaction from half life independence on initial concentration

questiontext.text: When initial concentration of a reactant is doubled in a reaction, its half-life period is not affected. The order of the reaction is

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
General relationship between half-life (\(t_{1/2}\)) and initial concentration (\([A]_0\)) for an \(n\)-th order reaction is:
\[ t_{1/2} \propto \frac{1}{[A]_0^{n-1}} \]

Evaluation:
For \(t_{1/2}\) to be completely independent of initial concentration \([A]_0\):
\[ n - 1 = 0 \implies n = 1 \]
For a first-order reaction, \(t_{1/2} = \frac{0.693}{k}\), which contains no initial concentration term.

Final Conclusion:
The order of the reaction is first order.
The correct order is first.

answer.text: more than zero but less than first.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q65 - Composition of equilibrium mixture with large equilibrium constant

questiontext.text: If the value of an equilibrium constant for a particular reaction is \(1.6 \times 10^{12}\), then at equilibrium the system will contain

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Equilibrium constant expression: \(K_{\text{eq}} = \frac{[\text{Products}]}{[\text{Reactants}]}\).

Evaluation:
A very high equilibrium constant value (\(K_{\text{eq}} = 1.6 \times 10^{12} \gg 10^3\)) indicates that the forward reaction proceeds nearly to completion before reaching equilibrium. Consequently, the equilibrium mixture consists almost entirely of products with negligible remaining reactants.

Final Conclusion:
At equilibrium, the system will contain mostly products.
The correct composition is mostly products.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q66 - Device converting combustion energy directly into electrical energy

questiontext.text: A device that converts energy of combustion of fuels like hydrogen and methane, directly into electrical energy is known as

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Galvanic cells designed to continuously convert the chemical energy of combustion of fuels (such as \(\text{H}_2\), \(\text{CH}_4\), or \(\text{CH}_3\text{OH}\)) directly into electrical energy are classified as fuel cells.

Evaluation:
For example, the hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell uses the combustion of hydrogen to generate electricity efficiently without thermal heat engine intermediary losses.

Final Conclusion:
The device is known as a fuel cell.
The correct device is a fuel cell.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q67 - Dissociation behavior from elevation in boiling point comparison

questiontext.text: The boiling point of \(0.2\mathrm{mol}\mathrm{kg}^{-1}\) solution of X in water is greater than equimolar solution of Y in water. Which one of the following statements is true in this case?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Elevation in boiling point formula: \(\Delta T_b = i K_b m\).

Evaluation:
For equimolar solutions (\(m_X = m_Y = 0.2\text{ mol kg}^{-1}\)) in the same solvent (water, constant \(K_b\)):
\[ \Delta T_b(X) > \Delta T_b(Y) \implies i_X > i_Y \]
A higher van 't Hoff factor (\(i_X > 1\)) indicates that solute X dissociates into a greater number of solute particles in water compared to solute Y.

Final Conclusion:
X is undergoing dissociation in water.
The true statement is that X is undergoing dissociation in water.

answer.text: Molecular mass of X is greater than the molecular mass of Y.
Molecular mass of X is less than the molecular mass of Y.
Y is undergoing dissociation in water while X undergoes no change.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q68 - Electrolyte with same Van t Hoff factor as aluminum sulfate

questiontext.text: Which one of the following electrolytes has same value of Van't Hoff's factor (i) as that of \(\mathrm{Al}_{2}(\mathrm{SO}_{4})_{3}\) (if all are \(100\%\) ionised)?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
For \(100\%\) ionization, the van 't Hoff factor \(i\) equals the total number of ions produced per formula unit of electrolyte.

Evaluation of Ionization:
1. \(\mathrm{Al}_2(\mathrm{SO}_4)_3 \to 2\mathrm{Al}^{3+} + 3\mathrm{SO}_4^{2-} \implies i = 2 + 3 = 5\).
2. \(\mathrm{K}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6] \to 4\mathrm{K}^+ + [\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{4-} \implies i = 4 + 1 = 5\).
3. \(\mathrm{K}_3[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6] \to 3\mathrm{K}^+ + [\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]^{3-} \implies i = 3 + 1 = 4\).
4. \(\mathrm{Al}(\mathrm{NO}_3)_3 \to \mathrm{Al}^{3+} + 3\mathrm{NO}_3^- \implies i = 1 + 3 = 4\).
5. \(\mathrm{K}_2\mathrm{SO}_4 \to 2\mathrm{K}^+ + \mathrm{SO}_4^{2-} \implies i = 2 + 1 = 3\).

Final Conclusion:
\(\mathrm{K}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]\) yields \(5\) ions upon complete ionization, matching \(\mathrm{Al}_2(\mathrm{SO}_4)_3\).
The correct electrolyte is \(\mathrm{K}_4[\mathrm{Fe}(\mathrm{CN})_6]\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q69 - Comparison of d electron count in ferrous ion with other species

questiontext.text: The number of \(d\)-electrons in \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) (\(Z = 26\)) is not equal to the number of electrons in which one of the following?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Count the subshell electron configurations for each species based on atomic numbers.

Step-by-Step Evaluation:
1. Number of d-electrons in \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) (\(Z = 26\)):
Electronic configuration of \(\mathrm{Fe} = [\mathrm{Ar}] 3\mathrm{d}^6 4\mathrm{s}^2\).
Electronic configuration of \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+} = [\mathrm{Ar}] 3\mathrm{d}^6 \implies 6\text{ d-electrons}\).
2. Compare with given species:
- s-electrons in \(\mathrm{Mg}\) (\(Z = 12\)): Configuration is \(1\mathrm{s}^2 2\mathrm{s}^2 2\mathrm{p}^6 3\mathrm{s}^2 \implies 2 + 2 + 2 = 6\text{ s-electrons}\).
- p-electrons in \(\mathrm{Ne}\) (\(Z = 10\)): Configuration is \(1\mathrm{s}^2 2\mathrm{s}^2 2\mathrm{p}^6 \implies 6\text{ p-electrons}\).
- d-electrons in \(\mathrm{Fe}\) (\(Z = 26\)): Configuration is \([\mathrm{Ar}] 3\mathrm{d}^6 4\mathrm{s}^2 \implies 6\text{ d-electrons}\).
- p-electrons in \(\mathrm{Cl}\) (\(Z = 17\)): Configuration is \(1\mathrm{s}^2 2\mathrm{s}^2 2\mathrm{p}^6 3\mathrm{s}^2 3\mathrm{p}^5 \implies 6 + 5 = 11\text{ p-electrons}\).

Final Conclusion:
The number of d-electrons in \(\mathrm{Fe}^{2+}\) (\(6\)) is not equal to the number of p-electrons in \(\mathrm{Cl}\) (\(11\)).
The correct choice is p-electrons in \(\mathrm{Cl}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q70 - Correct bond order sequence for dioxygen ions

questiontext.text: The correct bond order in the following species is

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Applying Molecular Orbital Theory for dioxygen ions:

Bond Order Calculations:
1. \(\mathrm{O}_2^{2+}\) (\(14\text{ electrons}\)): \(\text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 4}{2} = 3.0\).
2. \(\mathrm{O}_2^+\) (\(15\text{ electrons}\)): \(\text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 5}{2} = 2.5\).
3. \(\mathrm{O}_2^-\) (\(17\text{ electrons}\)): \(\text{Bond Order} = \frac{10 - 7}{2} = 1.5\).

Final Conclusion:
Comparing values: \(1.5 < 2.5 < 3.0\), which gives:
\[ \mathrm{O}_2^- < \mathrm{O}_2^+ < \mathrm{O}_2^{2+} \]
The correct order is \(\mathrm{O}_2^- < \mathrm{O}_2^+ < \mathrm{O}_2^{2+}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q71 - Orbital angular momentum of electron in d orbital

questiontext.text: The angular momentum of electrons in \(d\) orbital is equal to

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Orbital angular momentum formula:
\[ L = \sqrt{l(l + 1)} \hbar = \sqrt{l(l + 1)} \left(\frac{h}{2\pi}\right) \]

Step-by-Step Calculation:
For a \(d\)-orbital, azimuthal quantum number \(l = 2\):
\[ L = \sqrt{2(2 + 1)} \left(\frac{h}{2\pi}\right) = \sqrt{2 \times 3} \left(\frac{h}{2\pi}\right) = \sqrt{6}\left(\frac{h}{2\pi}\right) \]

Final Conclusion:
The orbital angular momentum of an electron in a \(d\)-orbital is \(\sqrt{6}\left(\frac{h}{2\pi}\right)\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q72 - Salt precipitating last from solubility product comparison

questiontext.text: The \(\mathrm{K}_{\mathrm{sp}}\) of \(\mathrm{Ag}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}_{4}\), \(\mathrm{AgCl}\), \(\mathrm{AgBr}\) and \(\mathrm{AgI}\) are respectively, \(1.1 \times 10^{-12}\), \(1.8 \times 10^{-10}\), \(5.0 \times 10^{-13}\), \(8.3 \times 10^{-17}\). Which one of the following salts will precipitate last if \(\mathrm{AgNO}_{3}\) solution is added to the solution containing equal moles of \(\mathrm{AgCl}\), \(\mathrm{AgBr}\), \(\mathrm{AgI}\), \(\mathrm{Ag}_{2}\mathrm{CrO}_{4}\)?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Precipitation begins when the ionic product exceeds \(K_{\text{sp}}\). The salt that requires the highest concentration of \(\mathrm{Ag}^+\) ions to exceed its solubility product will precipitate last.

Required \(\mathrm{Ag}^+\) Concentration Calculations:
Assuming equal molar anion concentration \(C\):
1. For \(\mathrm{AgI}\): \([\mathrm{Ag}^+] = \frac{K_{\text{sp}}}{C} = \frac{8.3 \times 10^{-17}}{C}\).
2. For \(\mathrm{AgBr}\): \([\mathrm{Ag}^+] = \frac{K_{\text{sp}}}{C} = \frac{5.0 \times 10^{-13}}{C}\).
3. For \(\mathrm{AgCl}\): \([\mathrm{Ag}^+] = \frac{K_{\text{sp}}}{C} = \frac{1.8 \times 10^{-10}}{C}\).
4. For \(\mathrm{Ag}_2\mathrm{CrO}_4\): \([\mathrm{Ag}^+]^2 C = 1.1 \times 10^{-12} \implies [\mathrm{Ag}^+] = \sqrt{\frac{1.1 \times 10^{-12}}{C}} \approx \frac{1.05 \times 10^{-6}}{\sqrt{C}}\).

Final Conclusion:
Since \(\sim 10^{-6}\text{ M}\) is much greater than \(10^{-10}\text{ M}\), \(\mathrm{Ag}_2\mathrm{CrO}_4\) requires the highest concentration of silver ions to start precipitating, and therefore precipitates last.
The salt that precipitates last is \(\mathrm{Ag}_2\mathrm{CrO}_4\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q73 - Colloidal property independent of particle electrical charge

questiontext.text: Which property of colloidal solution is independent of charge on the colloidal particles?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Electrical properties of colloids (such as coagulation, electrophoresis, and electro-osmosis) depend directly on the presence and magnitude of electric charges on the surface of colloidal particles.

Evaluation of Tyndall Effect:
Tyndall effect is an optical property caused by the scattering of light by colloidal particles due to their suitable size relative to the wavelength of light. It is completely independent of whether the particles carry a positive, negative, or neutral charge.

Final Conclusion:
Tyndall effect is independent of charge on colloidal particles.
The correct property is Tyndall effect.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q74 - Relation between standard Gibbs free energy change and equilibrium constant

questiontext.text: Which of the following statements is correct for a reversible process in a state of equilibrium?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
At equilibrium, the net Gibbs free energy change \(\Delta G = 0\). The relationship between standard Gibbs free energy change (\(\Delta G^\circ\)) and equilibrium constant (\(K\)) is given by thermodynamic principles.

Formula Derivation:
\[ \Delta G^\circ = -R T \ln K = -2.303 R T \log_{10} K \]

Final Conclusion:
The correct thermodynamic relation at equilibrium is \(\Delta G^\circ = -2.303 R T \log K\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q75 - Biological function of bithionol additive in soaps

questiontext.text: Bithionol is generally added to the soaps as an additive to function as a/an

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Bithionol (2,2'-thiobis(4,6-dichlorophenol)) is a chlorinated bisphenol derivative incorporated into medicated soaps.

Evaluation:
Bithionol possesses antibacterial properties that reduce bacterial growth on skin surfaces, thereby reducing odor caused by bacterial decomposition of organic substances in sweat. Hence, it functions as an antiseptic additive in soaps.

Final Conclusion:
Bithionol is added to soaps to function as an antiseptic.
The correct function is antiseptic.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q76 - Product of electrolytic reduction of nitrobenzene in strongly acidic medium

questiontext.text: The electrolytic reduction of nitrobenzene in strongly acidic medium produces

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Electrolytic reduction of nitrobenzene (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NO}_2\)) in strongly acidic medium initially forms phenylhydroxylamine (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NHOH}\)).

Reaction Mechanism:
In strongly acidic medium, phenylhydroxylamine rapidly undergoes an intramolecular acid-catalyzed rearrangement (Bamberger rearrangement) to convert into \(p\)-aminophenol (\(\text{HO-C}_6\text{H}_4\text{-NH}_2\)).

Final Conclusion:
The product obtained from electrolytic reduction of nitrobenzene in strongly acidic medium is \(p\)-aminophenol.
The correct product is \(p\)-aminophenol.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q77 - Percentage of nitrogen in organic compound using Dumas method

questiontext.text: In Duma's method for estimation of nitrogen, 0.25 g of an organic compound gave \(40~\mathrm{mL}\) of nitrogen collected at \(300\mathrm{K}\) temperature and \(725\mathrm{mm}\) pressure. If the aqueous tension at \(300\mathrm{K}\) is \(25\mathrm{mm}\), the percentage of nitrogen in the compound is

generalfeedback.text:
Given Data and Conditions:
Mass of organic compound \(m = 0.25\text{ g}\).
Volume of moist nitrogen \(V_1 = 40\text{ mL}\).
Temperature \(T_1 = 300\text{ K}\).
Total pressure \(P = 725\text{ mm Hg}\).
Aqueous tension \(p = 25\text{ mm Hg}\).

Assumptions and Sign Conventions:
Nitrogen gas obeys ideal gas law. Standard pressure \(P_0 = 760\text{ mm Hg}\), standard temperature \(T_0 = 273\text{ K}\).

Relevant Formulae and Principles:
1. Pressure of dry nitrogen gas: \(P_1 = P - p = 725 - 25 = 700\text{ mm Hg}\).
2. Ideal gas volume reduction to STP: \(V_0 = \frac{P_1 V_1 T_0}{P_0 T_1}\).
3. Percentage of nitrogen: \(\%\text{ N} = \frac{28}{22400} \times \frac{V_0}{m} \times 100\).

Step-by-Step Working:
1. Calculate volume of dry nitrogen at STP (\(V_0\)):
\[ V_0 = \frac{700 \times 40 \times 273}{760 \times 300} = \frac{7644000}{228000} = 33.526\text{ mL} \]
2. Calculate percentage of nitrogen:
\[ \%\text{ N} = \frac{28}{22400} \times \frac{33.526}{0.25} \times 100 = 0.00125 \times 134.104 \times 100 = 16.76\% \]

Check and Final Answer:
Checking steps: \(33.526 / 22400 \times 28 = 0.0419\text{ g N}_2\), \((0.0419 / 0.25) \times 100 = 16.76\%\).
The percentage of nitrogen in the compound is \(16.76\%\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q78 - Compound yielding most stable carbocation upon C-Cl bond ionization

questiontext.text: In which of the following compounds, the C-Cl bond ionisation shall give most stable carbonium ion?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Carbocation stability is enhanced by resonance delocalization, hyperconjugation, inductive effects, and aromaticity (Hückel's \(4n+2\) \(\pi\)-electron rule).

Evaluation of Ionization Products:
Ionization of the \(\text{C-Cl}\) bond in cycloheptatrienyl chloride (tropylium chloride) generates the tropylium carbocation (\(\text{C}_7\text{H}_7^+\)). The tropylium cation contains \(6\) \(\pi\)-electrons completely delocalized in a planar 7-membered ring, satisfying Hückel's rule (\(4n+2\) for \(n=1\)). This aromatic stabilization makes it exceptionally stable compared to aliphatic, tertiary, or benzylic carbocations.

Final Conclusion:
Ionization of cycloheptatrienyl chloride yields the aromatic tropylium cation, which is the most stable carbonium ion.
The compound that gives the most stable carbonium ion is cycloheptatrienyl chloride.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q79 - Identification of organic reaction between sodium salt and alkyl halide

questiontext.text:
The reaction,

\[ \mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\text{-C(ONa)}=\mathrm{CH}_2 + \mathrm{CH}_{3}\mathrm{CH}_{2}\mathrm{Cl} \xrightarrow{-\mathrm{NaCl}} \mathrm{CH}_{3}\text{-C(O-CH}_2\mathrm{CH}_3)=\mathrm{CH}_2 \]

is called

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
The reaction between a sodium alkoxide / enolate (\(\mathrm{R}\text{-O}^-\mathrm{Na}^+\)) and a primary alkyl halide (\(\mathrm{R}'\text{-X}\)) to form an ether (\(\mathrm{R}\text{-O-R}'\)) with the elimination of sodium halide (\(\mathrm{NaX}\)) proceeds via an \(\text{S}_\text{N}2\) nucleophilic substitution mechanism.

Evaluation:
This organic reaction method for the preparation of ethers from an alkoxide/enolate ion and an alkyl halide is known as Williamson synthesis.

Final Conclusion:
The reaction is named Williamson synthesis.
The correct reaction name is Williamson synthesis.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q80 - Electrophilic addition of hydrobromic acid to 1-phenylpropene

questiontext.text: The reaction of \(\mathrm{C_6H_5CH = CHCH_3}\) with HBr produces

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Electrophilic addition of \(\text{HBr}\) to an unsymmetrical alkene proceeds via the most stable carbocation intermediate according to Markovnikov's rule.

Reaction Mechanism:
1. Protonation (\(\text{H}^+\) addition) at the double bond can yield two possible carbocations:
- Secondary carbocation: \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CH}_2\text{-}\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H-CH}_3\).
- Benzylic carbocation: \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-}\overset{+}{\text{C}}\text{H-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3\).
2. The benzylic carbocation is stabilized by extensive resonance delocalization with the adjacent benzene ring, making it significantly more stable.
3. Nucleophilic attack by bromide ion (\(\text{Br}^-\)) occurs at the benzylic carbon to yield 1-bromo-1-phenylpropane (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{CH(Br)CH}_2\text{CH}_3\)).

Final Conclusion:
The reaction produces \(\mathrm{C_6H_5CH(Br)CH_2CH_3}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q81 - Ozonolysis of cyclic alkene yielding dicarbonyl compound

questiontext.text:
A single compound of the structure

is obtainable from ozonolysis of which of the following cyclic compounds?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Reductive ozonolysis of a cyclic alkene cleaves the double bond (\(\text{C=C}\)) to yield a single open-chain dicarbonyl compound containing aldehyde and/or ketone functional groups at the former double-bond carbons.

Evaluation of Ozonolysis:
1. The product is 6-oxo-3-methylheptanal: \(\text{OHC-CH}_2\text{-CH(CH}_3\text{)-CH}_2\text{-CO-CH}_3\).
2. Reconnecting the carbonyl carbon of the aldehyde group (\(\text{-CHO}\)) and the carbonyl carbon of the ketone group (\(\text{-CO-CH}_3\)) through a double bond reforms the 5-membered cyclic alkene ring.
3. Joining \(\text{C1}\) (aldehyde carbon) and \(\text{C6}\) (ketone carbon) yields 1,4-dimethylcyclopentene.

Final Conclusion:
Ozonolysis of 1,4-dimethylcyclopentene yields the target dicarbonyl compound.
The correct cyclic compound is 1,4-dimethylcyclopentene.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q82 - Reaction of cyclopentanone with methyl lithium

questiontext.text: Treatment of cyclopentanone with methyl lithium gives which of the following species?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Methyl lithium (\(\text{CH}_3\text{Li}\)) is a strong organometallic base as well as a strong nucleophile. When reacting with ketones containing acidic \(\alpha\)-hydrogens, it can act as a base to abstract an \(\alpha\)-proton.

Evaluation:
Deprotonation of an \(\alpha\)-hydrogen from cyclopentanone by the methyl anion of \(\text{CH}_3\text{Li}\) yields the resonance-stabilized cyclopentanonyl enolate anion (cyclopentanonyl anion) alongside methane gas (\(\text{CH}_4\)).

Final Conclusion:
The reaction generates the cyclopentanonyl anion.
The correct species is cyclopentanonyl anion.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q83 - Hyperconjugation in organic free radicals

questiontext.text:
Consider the following compounds

Hyperconjugation occurs in

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Hyperconjugation in free radicals requires the presence of \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atoms (\(\text{C-H}\) \(\sigma\)-bonds) adjacent to the carbon atom carrying the unpaired electron.

Structural Analysis:
1. Radical I: The radical carbon is attached to a tert-butyl group (\(\text{-C(CH}_3)_3\)) which has zero \(\alpha\)-hydrogens on that quaternary carbon, and a phenyl ring where delocalization occurs by resonance rather than hyperconjugation.
2. Radical II: Triphenylmethyl radical contains zero \(\alpha\)-hydrogens on the central radical carbon; stabilization occurs exclusively via resonance.
3. Radical III: The radical carbon is bonded to an adjacent carbon carrying a methyl group and \(\alpha\)-hydrogens, permitting \(\sigma\text{-p}\) orbital overlap (hyperconjugation).

Final Conclusion:
Hyperconjugation occurs only in Radical III.
The correct choice is III only.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q84 - Electron displacement representation for nucleophilic substitution

questiontext.text: Which of the following is the most correct electron displacement for a nucleophilic reaction to take place?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Curved arrows in organic reaction mechanisms represent the movement of electron pairs from electron-rich regions (like \(\pi\)-bonds or inductive donor methyl groups) toward electron-deficient carbons or electronegative leaving groups.

Evaluation of Electron Displacement:
In 1-chlorobut-2-ene (\(\text{H}_3\text{C-CH=CH-CH}_2\text{-Cl}\)):
1. The electron-donating methyl group (\(\text{H}_3\text{C}\rightarrow\)) exerts a \(+\text{I}\) effect.
2. The \(\pi\)-electrons of the double bond shift toward the next carbon–carbon bond (\(\text{CH}=\text{CH}\rightarrow\text{CH}_2\)).
3. The electronegative chlorine atom withdraws the bonding electron pair (\(\rightarrow\text{Cl}\)) as a chloride leaving group.
This sequence correctly represents allylic electron displacement facilitating nucleophilic substitution.

Final Conclusion:
The correct representation shows electron displacement propagating from the methyl group through the double bond to the chlorine atom leaving group.
The correct representation is \(\mathrm{H_3C} \rightarrow \mathrm{H}\mathrm{C} = \mathrm{C} - \mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cl}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q85 - Number of sigma and pi bonds in ethyl acetoacetate enol

questiontext.text: The enolic form of ethyl acetoacetate as given below has

generalfeedback.text:
Given Data and Conditions:
Enolic structure of ethyl acetoacetate: \(\text{CH}_3\text{-C(OH)=CH-C(=O)-O-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3\).

Step-by-Step Bond Counting:
1. Molecular formula: \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{10}\text{O}_3\).
2. Count \(\sigma\)-bonds:
- \(\text{C-H}\) single \(\sigma\)-bonds = 10
- \(\text{C-C}\) single/double \(\sigma\)-bonds = 5
- \(\text{C-O}\) single/double \(\sigma\)-bonds = 2
- \(\text{O-H}\) single \(\sigma\)-bond = 1
Total \(\sigma\)-bonds = \(10 + 5 + 2 + 1 = 18\).
3. Count \(\pi\)-bonds:
- \(1\) double bond \(\text{C=C}\) contains \(1\pi\)-bond.
- \(1\) double bond \(\text{C=O}\) contains \(1\pi\)-bond.
Total \(\pi\)-bonds = \(2\).

Check and Final Answer:
The structure contains 18 \(\sigma\)-bonds and 2 \(\pi\)-bonds.
The enolic form of ethyl acetoacetate has 18 \(\sigma\)-bonds and 2 \(\pi\)-bonds.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_Q86 - Keto enol tautomerism in unsaturated cyclic ketones

questiontext.text:
Given,

(III)

Which of the given compounds can exhibit tautomerism?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Keto-enol tautomerism requires the presence of at least one acidic \(\alpha\)-hydrogen atom adjacent to the carbonyl group (\(\text{C=O}\)), or an \(\alpha\)-hydrogen capable of conjugated enolization through a double bond (\(\gamma\)-hydrogen enolization).

Evaluation of Compounds:
1. Compound I: Contains acidic \(\alpha\)-hydrogens at the \(\text{C6}\) position relative to the carbonyl group, allowing enolization.
2. Compound II: Contains acidic \(\alpha\)-hydrogens at the \(\text{C5}\) position, allowing conjugated enolization.
3. Compound III: Contains acidic \(\alpha\)-hydrogens at the \(\text{C6}\) position, allowing enolization.
Therefore, all three compounds (I, II, and III) possess enolizable hydrogens and exhibit tautomerism.

Final Conclusion:
All three given compounds I, II, and III can exhibit tautomerism.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_MCQ_Q87 - Order of enthalpy of hydrogenation of alkenes

questiontext.text:
The enthalpy of hydrogenation of these compounds will be in the order as:

(III)

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Enthalpy of hydrogenation (\(\Delta H_{\text{hydro}}\)) is the heat released during the catalytic addition of hydrogen to unsaturated double bonds. For alkenes with the same degree of unsaturation, the enthalpy of hydrogenation is inversely proportional to the thermodynamic stability of the alkene. A less stable alkene has higher potential energy and releases more heat upon hydrogenation.

Evaluation:
Compound II has non-conjugated, isolated or strained double bonds making it the least stable, hence it exhibits the highest enthalpy of hydrogenation. Compound III has an intermediate stability due to partial hyperconjugation/conjugation. Compound I possesses maximum conjugation and hyperconjugation, making it the most stable alkene with the lowest enthalpy of hydrogenation.

Final Conclusion:
The decreasing order of enthalpy of hydrogenation is \(\text{II} > \text{III} > \text{I}\).

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_MCQ_Q88 - Biodegradable polymer formed from glycine and aminocaproic acid

questiontext.text: Biodegradable polymer which can be produced from glycine and aminocaproic acid is

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Polymers derived from amino acids or hydroxy acids contain functional linkages (like amide or ester bonds) that can be degraded by enzymes or microorganisms in nature.

Evaluation:
Copolymerization of glycine (\(\text{H}_2\text{N-CH}_2\text{-COOH}\)) and \(\epsilon\)-aminocaproic acid (\(\text{H}_2\text{N-(CH}_2\text{)}_5\text{-COOH}\)) forms nylon 2-nylon 6, a biodegradable polyamide copolymer. Poly \(\beta\)-hydroxybutyrate-co-\(\beta\)-hydroxyvalerate (PHBV) is produced from 3-hydroxybutanoic acid and 3-hydroxypentanoic acid. Buna-N and nylon-6,6 are non-biodegradable synthetic polymers.

Final Conclusion:
The biodegradable polymer produced from glycine and aminocaproic acid is nylon 2-nylon 6.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_MCQ_Q89 - Total number of pi bond electrons in structure

questiontext.text: The total number of \(\pi\)-bond electrons in the following structure is

generalfeedback.text:
Given Data and Conditions:
A conjugated organic polyene structure is given.

Relevant Formulae and Principles:
1. Every double bond consists of one \(\sigma\) bond and one \(\pi\) bond.
2. Each \(\pi\) bond contains two shared \(\pi\)-electrons.

Step-by-Step Working:
Counting the double bonds in the given structure reveals exactly 4 double bonds (\(\text{C=C}\)).
Number of \(\pi\) bonds = 4.
Total number of \(\pi\)-electrons = \(4 \times 2 = 8\).

Check and Final Answer:
4 double bonds contain 8 \(\pi\)-electrons. Thus, the total number of \(\pi\)-bond electrons is 8.

name.text: NEET_UG_CHEMISTRY_2015_MCQ_Q90 - Identification of organic compound X

questiontext.text: An organic compound X having molecular formula \(\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}\) yields phenyl hydrazone and gives negative response to the Iodoform test and Tollen's test. It produces \(n\)-pentane on reduction. X could be

generalfeedback.text:
Given Data and Conditions:
Molecular formula = \(\text{C}_5\text{H}_{10}\text{O}\).
Reactions: Forms phenyl hydrazone, negative Tollen's test, negative Iodoform test, yields \(n\)-pentane on reduction.

Step-by-Step Evaluation:
1. Formation of phenyl hydrazone indicates the presence of a carbonyl group (\(\text{C=O}\)).
2. Negative Tollen's test shows that X is a ketone, not an aldehyde (eliminating pentanal).
3. Negative Iodoform test indicates that X is not a methyl ketone, meaning it lacks a \(\text{CH}_3\text{C=O}\) group (eliminating 2-pentanone).
4. Reduction to \(n\)-pentane confirms an unbranched 5-carbon skeleton.
5. Among the 5-carbon unbranched ketones, 3-pentanone (\(\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{COCH}_2\text{CH}_3\)) fits all given chemical tests.

Final Conclusion:
The organic compound X is 3-pentanone.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q91 - Correct matching of fungal class and characteristics

questiontext.text:
Which one of the following matches is correct?

OptionOrganismFeatureClass
(a)PhytophthoraAseptate myceliumBasidiomycetes
(b)AlternariaSexual reproduction absentDeuteromycetes
(c)MucorReproduction by conjugationAscomycetes
(d)AgaricusParasitic fungusBasidiomycetes

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Fungi are classified into distinct classes based on mycelium morphology, mode of spore formation, and fruiting bodies.

Evaluation:
1. Phytophthora belongs to Phycomycetes (Oomycetes), not Basidiomycetes.
2. Alternaria belongs to Deuteromycetes (imperfect fungi) because its sexual stage is absent or unknown. This match is completely correct.
3. Mucor belongs to Phycomycetes (Zygomycetes), not Ascomycetes.
4. Agaricus is a saprophytic fungus (mushroom), not a parasitic fungus.

Final Conclusion:
The correct match is Alternaria — Sexual reproduction absent — Deuteromycetes.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q92 - Identification of correct statements on plant kingdom

questiontext.text:
Read the following five statements (I to V) and select the option with all the correct statements.

I. Mosses and lichens are the first organisms to colonise a bare rock.
II. Selaginella is a homosporous pteridophyte.
III. Coralloid roots in Cycas have VAM.
IV. Main plant body in bryophytes is gametophytic, whereas in pteridophytes it is sporophytic.
V. In gymnosperms, male and female gametophytes are present within sporangia located on sporophyte.

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Evaluation of botanical principles across plant groups:

Statement Evaluation:
Statement I is correct: Mosses and lichens are pioneer species in primary succession on bare rocks.
Statement II is incorrect: Selaginella is heterosporous (produces microspores and megaspores).
Statement III is incorrect: Coralloid roots of Cycas harbor nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria (such as Anabaena cycadae), not Vesicular Arbuscular Mycorrhizae (VAM).
Statement IV is correct: Bryophytes have a dominant gametophytic generation, while pteridophytes have a dominant sporophytic generation.
Statement V is correct: In gymnosperms, male and female gametophytes lack independent free-living existence and remain retained within sporangia located on the sporophyte.

Final Conclusion:
Statements I, IV, and V are correct.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q93 - Non independent free living gametophyte

questiontext.text: Which of the following gametophyte is not independent free-living?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
In plant evolution, the gametophytic phase transitions from being dominant and independent (in bryophytes and pteridophytes) to being highly reduced, dependent, and non-free-living (in gymnosperms and angiosperms).

Evaluation:
Funaria and Marchantia (bryophytes) have independent, dominant gametophytes. Pteris (pteridophyte) has an independent, free-living, photosynthetic prothallus. In Pinus (gymnosperm), the gametophyte is highly reduced and remains retained within the sporangia on the sporophyte, lacking an independent free-living existence.

Final Conclusion:
The gametophyte of Pinus is not independent free-living.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q94 - Incorrect statement regarding algal products and stored food

questiontext.text: Which one of the following statements is wrong?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Algal classes differ in their dominant pigments, stored food materials, and cell wall compositions.

Evaluation:
- Algin (from brown algae) and carrageenan (from red algae) are commercially important hydrocolloids.
- Agar-agar is a gel-like substance extracted from red algae such as Gelidium and Gracilaria.
- Chlorella and Spirulina are unicellular protein-rich algae used as food supplements by space travellers.
- Mannitol is a complex carbohydrate storage product of Phaeophyceae (brown algae). Rhodophyceae (red algae) store reserve food as Floridean starch, which is structurally similar to amylopectin and glycogen. Therefore, stating that mannitol is the stored food of Rhodophyceae is incorrect.

Final Conclusion:
The statement "Mannitol is the stored food of Rhodophyceae" is wrong.

answer.text: Mannitol is the stored food of Rhodophyceae.
Algin and carrageenan are products of algae.
Chlorella and Spirulina are used as space food.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q95 - Presence of methanogens in ruminant guts

questiontext.text: The guts of cow and buffalo possess

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Methanogens are specialized obligate anaerobic archaebacteria present in the digestive tract of ruminant animals.

Evaluation:
Methanogenic archaebacteria break down cellulose anaerobically in the rumen of cows and buffaloes, producing methane gas (\(\text{CH}_4\)). Fucus, Chlorella, and cyanobacteria are photosynthetic organisms not present in ruminant guts.

Final Conclusion:
The guts of cow and buffalo possess methanogens.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q96 - Flagellated male gametes in algae

questiontext.text: Male gametes are flagellated in

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Motility of male gametes varies among different algal groups based on flagellar features.

Evaluation:
Ectocarpus (brown algae / Phaeophyceae) produces biflagellated, heterokont male gametes with lateral flagella. Polysiphonia (red algae / Rhodophyceae) has non-motile gametes. Anabaena (cyanobacteria) lacks flagellated cells. Spirogyra (green algae) reproduces by conjugation involving non-flagellated amoeboid gametes.

Final Conclusion:
Male gametes are flagellated in Ectocarpus.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q97 - Reason for closed vascular bundles in monocots

questiontext.text: Vascular bundles in monocotyledons are considered closed because

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
A vascular bundle is defined as 'open' if cambium is present between xylem and phloem (allowing secondary growth) and 'closed' if cambium is absent.

Evaluation:
In monocotyledonous stems and roots, intra-fascicular cambium is absent between xylem and phloem tissues. Because secondary vascular tissues cannot be produced, the vascular bundles are described as closed.

Final Conclusion:
Vascular bundles in monocots are closed because cambium is absent.

answer.text: xylem is surrounded all around by phloem.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q98 - Floral formula of Petunia

questiontext.text: \(\oplus \boldsymbol{\Phi} K_{(5)} C_{(5)} A_5 \underline{G}_{(2)}\) is the floral formula of

generalfeedback.text:
Given Data and Interpretation:
\(\oplus\): Actinomorphic symmetry.
\(\boldsymbol{\Phi}\): Bisexual flower.
\(K_{(5)}\): Calyx with 5 fused sepals.
\(C_{(5)}\): Corolla with 5 fused petals.
\(A_5\): 5 epipetalous stamens.
\(\underline{G}_{(2)}\): Superior ovary with 2 fused carpels (bicarpellary syncarpous).

Evaluation:
This formula represents the Solanaceae family. Petunia is a representative member of Solanaceae. Allium belongs to Liliaceae, Sesbania to Fabaceae, and Brassica to Brassicaceae.

Final Conclusion:
The given floral formula belongs to Petunia.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q99 - Major characteristic of monocot root

questiontext.text: A major characteristic of the monocot root is the presence of

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Monocot roots possess radial, closed vascular bundles with polyarch xylem (more than six xylem bundles) and a large, well-developed pith, without any cambium.

Evaluation:
Because cambium is absent in monocot roots, no secondary growth occurs, making "vasculature without cambium" a defining feature. Open vascular bundles and cambium rings are characteristic of dicot roots/stems. Scattered vascular bundles are characteristic of monocot stems, not monocot roots.

Final Conclusion:
A major characteristic of the monocot root is vasculature without cambium.

answer.text: cambium sandwiched between phloem and xylem along the radius.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q100 - Keel characteristic feature of Indigofera flower

questiontext.text: Keel is the characteristic feature of flower of

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
In papilionaceous aestivation (characteristic of the Fabaceae family), the corolla consists of five petals: one large posterior standard (vexillum), two lateral wings (alae), and two innermost fused petals forming a boat-shaped structure called the keel (carina).

Evaluation:
Indigofera belongs to the Fabaceae family and possesses a keel petal structure. Tulip and Aloe belong to Liliaceae (tepals/perianth). Tomato belongs to Solanaceae (valvate aestivation).

Final Conclusion:
Keel is a characteristic feature of the flower of Indigofera.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q101 - Perigynous flowers in rose

questiontext.text: Perigynous flowers are found in

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Based on the position of floral parts with respect to the ovary on the thalamus, flowers are classified as hypogynous (superior ovary), perigynous (half-inferior ovary), or epigynous (inferior ovary).

Evaluation:
In perigynous flowers, the thalamus forms a cup-shaped or rim-like receptacle around the ovary, and other floral whorls arise on the margin of the thalamus at the same level. Examples include rose, plum, and peach. Guava and cucumber have epigynous flowers. China rose has hypogynous flowers.

Final Conclusion:
Perigynous flowers are found in rose.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q102 - Leaf modification into spines in Opuntia

questiontext.text: Leaves become modified into spines in

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Leaves undergo morphological modifications to adapt to environmental stresses such as drought or herbivory.

Evaluation:
In xerophytic plants like Opuntia (prickly pear), leaves are modified into sharp, pointed spines to minimize transpirational water loss and protect against herbivores, while the stem becomes green and photosynthetic (phylloclade). In pea, leaves modify into tendrils. In onion, fleshy leaves store food. In silk cotton, leaves are palmately compound.

Final Conclusion:
Leaves are modified into spines in Opuntia.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q103 - Stacking of membranous sacs as grana in chloroplasts

questiontext.text: The structures that are formed by stacking of organised flattened membranous sacs in the chloroplasts are

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
The internal matrix of chloroplasts contains membrane-bound sacs where light-dependent reactions of photosynthesis occur.

Evaluation:
Flattened membranous sacs called thylakoids are arranged in stacks like piles of coins to form grana (singular: granum). Stroma lamellae connect different grana stacks. Cristae are infoldings of the inner mitochondrial membrane. Stroma is the fluid matrix surrounding thylakoids.

Final Conclusion:
The structures formed by stacking of flattened membranous sacs are grana.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q104 - Acrocentric chromosome with centromere near one end

questiontext.text: The chromosomes in which centromere is situated close to one end are

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Chromosomes are classified into four types based on the position of the centromere (primary constriction):

Evaluation:
1. Metacentric: Centromere in the middle, forming two equal arms.
2. Sub-metacentric: Centromere slightly away from the center, forming one shorter and one longer arm.
3. Acrocentric: Centromere situated extremely close to one end, forming one extremely short arm and one very long arm.
4. Telocentric: Centromere situated at the terminal end.

Final Conclusion:
Chromosomes with centromere situated close to one end are acrocentric.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q105 - Correct matching of ER types and functions

questiontext.text: Select the correct matching in the following pairs.

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
The Endoplasmic Reticulum (ER) is divided structurally and functionally into Smooth Endoplasmic Reticulum (SER) and Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum (RER). SER lacks ribosomes and is the principal site for lipid, phospholipid, and steroid hormone synthesis. RER is studded with ribosomes and is involved in protein synthesis and secretion.

Evaluation:
Smooth ER functions primarily in the synthesis of lipids. Glycogen synthesis occurs in the cytoplasm, while fatty acid oxidation occurs mainly in mitochondria and peroxisomes.

Final Conclusion:
The correct matching pair is Smooth ER — Synthesis of lipids.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q106 - Absence of true nucleus in Anabaena

questiontext.text: True nucleus is absent in

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Prokaryotes lack a nuclear membrane-enclosed true nucleus and membrane-bound organelle systems, possessing instead an incipient nucleus (nucleoid). Eukaryotes possess a membrane-bound nucleus.

Evaluation:
Anabaena is a cyanobacterium (prokaryote), so a true nucleus is absent. Mucor (fungus), Vaucheria (xanthophyte alga), and Volvox (green alga) are eukaryotic organisms possessing true membrane-bound nuclei.

Final Conclusion:
A true nucleus is absent in Anabaena.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q107 - Non inclusion body in prokaryotes

questiontext.text: Which one of the following is not an inclusion body found in prokaryotes?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Inclusion bodies are non-membrane-bound reserve storage materials lying free in the cytoplasm of prokaryotic cells (such as phosphate granules, cyanophycean granules, and glycogen granules).

Evaluation:
A polysome (polyribosome) is a functional protein-synthesizing structure consisting of a mRNA strand bound to multiple ribosomes, rather than a storage inclusion body.

Final Conclusion:
Polysome is not an inclusion body found in prokaryotes.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q108 - Water ascent by transpiration pull and root pressure

questiontext.text: Transpiration and root pressure causes water to rise in plants by

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Water movement up the stem xylem is driven by two main physical forces: negative pressure (suction pull) generated at the leaf surface by transpiration, and positive pressure (hydrostatic push) generated at the root cortex by active ion absorption.

Evaluation:
Transpiration creates a transpiration pull that pulls water upwards from the top, whereas root pressure generates a positive pressure that pushes water upwards from the bottom. Therefore, transpiration and root pressure drive ascent of sap by pulling and pushing water, respectively.

Final Conclusion:
Transpiration and root pressure cause water to rise by pulling and pushing it, respectively.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q109 - Macronutrients required in large amounts for plant growth

questiontext.text: Minerals known to be required in large amounts for plant growth include

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Essential plant nutrients are categorized as macronutrients (required in large quantities, \(> 10\text{ mmole kg}^{-1}\) of dry matter) and micronutrients (required in trace amounts, \(< 10\text{ mmole kg}^{-1}\) of dry matter).

Evaluation:
Macronutrients include carbon, hydrogen, oxygen, nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium, calcium, magnesium, and sulphur. Phosphorus, potassium, sulphur, and calcium are all macronutrients. Elements such as manganese, copper, boron, zinc, and iron are micronutrients.

Final Conclusion:
Minerals required in large amounts include phosphorus, potassium, sulphur, and calcium.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q110 - Auxin role in phototropic bending of shoot

questiontext.text: What causes a green plant exposed to the light on only one side, to bend towards the source of light as it grows?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Phototropism is a directional growth response governed by asymmetrical plant hormone distribution (auxins).

Evaluation:
When a shoot tip receives unilateral light, auxin (indole-3-acetic acid) migrates to and accumulates on the shaded side. Higher auxin concentration on the shaded side stimulates greater cell elongation compared to the illuminated side, causing the shoot tip to bend toward the light source.

Final Conclusion:
The plant bends toward light because auxin accumulates on the shaded side, stimulating increased cell elongation there.

answer.text: Auxin accumulates on the shaded side, stimulating increased cell elongation there.
Green plants need light to perform photosynthesis.
Green plants seek light because they are phototropic.
Light stimulates plant cells on the lighted side to grow faster.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q111 - Root death in ring girdled plant

questiontext.text: In a ring girdled plant

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Girdling experiments demonstrate that phloem is the tissue responsible for downward translocation of organic food (photosynthates) from leaves to roots.

Evaluation:
When a ring of bark down to the phloem layer is removed around the trunk, organic food transport to the root system is completely severed. Starved of nutrient energy, the roots die first. Consequently, water uptake stops, leading to shoot death later.

Final Conclusion:
In a ring girdled plant, the root dies first.

answer.text: neither the root nor the shoot will die.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q112 - Sigmoid growth curve in plants

questiontext.text: Typical growth curve in plants is

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Plant growth under natural conditions follows a characteristic S-shaped (sigmoid) curve when total plant biomass/size is plotted against time.

Evaluation:
The sigmoid growth curve exhibits three sequential phases: an initial slow lag phase, a rapid exponential (log) phase, and a plateauing stationary phase due to limited nutrient availability.

Final Conclusion:
The typical growth curve in plants is sigmoid.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q113 - Potassium influx and efflux theory of stomatal movement

questiontext.text: Which one gives the most valid and recent explanation for stomatal movements?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Stomatal opening and closing are governed by turgor changes in guard cells caused by osmotically active solute movement across membranes.

Evaluation:
The active \(\text{K}^+\) influx and efflux theory proposed by Levitt is the widely accepted modern mechanism. Active uptake of \(\text{K}^+\) ions into guard cells lowers their osmotic potential, driving endosmosis and causing guard cells to swell and open the stoma. Efflux of \(\text{K}^+\) ions causes exosmosis and stomatal closure.

Final Conclusion:
The most valid explanation for stomatal movement is Potassium influx and efflux.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q114 - Definition of hilum as funicle attachment scar

questiontext.text: The hilum is a scar on the

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
The seed coat carries specific morphological features representing points of attachment and developmental pore structures of the original ovule.

Evaluation:
The hilum is a scar on the seed coat that marks the precise point where the seed was attached to its stalk (the funicle) during development within the fruit.

Final Conclusion:
The hilum is a scar on the seed, where funicle was attached.

answer.text: fruit, where it was attached to pedicel.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q115 - Geitonogamy functional cross pollination with genetic autogamy

questiontext.text: Which one of the following may require pollinators, but is genetically similar to autogamy?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Modes of pollination are classified functionally based on vector reliance and genetically based on pollen origin.

Evaluation:
Geitonogamy is the transfer of pollen grains from the anther of one flower to the stigma of another flower on the same plant. Functionally, it relies on pollinating agents (cross-pollination); however, genetically, it is equivalent to autogamy because pollen grains originate from the exact same plant genome.

Final Conclusion:
Geitonogamy requires pollinators but is genetically similar to autogamy.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q116 - False statement regarding honey formation from nectar

questiontext.text: Which one of the following statements is not true?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Analysis of pollination biology, pollen products, and apiculture principles:

Evaluation:
- Pollen grains are nutrient-dense structures used as health supplements in tablets and syrups.
- Pollen grains of plants like Parthenium cause severe respiratory allergies.
- Flowers pollinated by flies and beetles secrete foul odors to attract these pollinators.
- Honey is produced by honeybees from floral nectar (sugary secretions) via enzymatic inversion and evaporation, not by digesting collected pollen grains.

Final Conclusion:
The statement "Honey is made by bees after digesting pollen collected from flowers" is not true.

answer.text: Honey is made by bees after digesting pollen collected from flowers.
Pollen grain are rich in nutrients and they are used in the form of tablets and syrups.
Pollen grains of some plants causes severe allergies and bronchial afflictions in some people.
The flowers pollinated by flies and bats secrete foul odour to attract them.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q117 - Transmission tissue feature of solid style

questiontext.text: Transmission tissue is characteristic feature of

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Styles in angiosperms are categorized morphologically as hollow (open) or solid (closed).

Evaluation:
In solid styles, the center is filled with specialized transmitting (transmission) tissue composed of parenchymatous cells with intercellular spaces rich in mucilage, providing nutrients and guidance for growing pollen tubes.

Final Conclusion:
Transmission tissue is a characteristic feature of a solid style.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q118 - Vegetative propagation via rhizome in ginger

questiontext.text: In ginger, vegetative propagation occurs through

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Plants utilize modified vegetative structures (vegetative propagules) for asexual multiplication.

Evaluation:
In ginger (*Zingiber officinale*), vegetative propagation occurs via an underground modified stem called a rhizome, which bears nodes, internodes, and auxiliary buds that develop into new aerial shoots.

Final Conclusion:
In ginger, vegetative propagation occurs through a rhizome.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q119 - Nectar and pollen grains as floral rewards

questiontext.text: Which of the following are the important floral rewards to the animal pollinators?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Zoophilous flowers offer nutritive incentives (floral rewards) to animal pollinators to ensure repeated visitation and successful cross-pollination.

Evaluation:
Nectar (sugar-rich fluid) and pollen grains (protein-rich food) are the primary nutritional rewards provided by flowers to animal pollinators.

Final Conclusion:
The important floral rewards are nectar and pollen grains.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q120 - Seven contrasting character pairs studied by Mendel

questiontext.text: How many pairs of contrasting characters in pea plants were studied by Mendel in his experiments?

generalfeedback.text:
Given Data:
Mendel selected true-breeding garden pea (*Pisum sativum*) plants for hybridization studies.

Step-by-Step Evaluation:
Mendel analyzed exactly seven pairs of contrasting traits: stem height (tall/dwarf), flower color (violet/white), flower position (axial/terminal), pod shape (inflated/constricted), pod color (green/yellow), seed shape (round/wrinkled), and seed color (yellow/green).

Final Conclusion:
Mendel studied seven pairs of contrasting characters in pea plants.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q121 - Recombination as main mechanism of genetic variation

questiontext.text: Which is the most common mechanism of genetic variation in the population of a sexually reproducing organism?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Sexual reproduction generates genetic diversity through meiotic mechanisms that shuffle parental alleles.

Evaluation:
Genetic recombination (crossing over during pachytene of prophase I and independent assortment of homologous chromosomes during meiosis) is the most frequent and universal source of genetic variation in sexually reproducing populations.

Final Conclusion:
Recombination is the most common mechanism of genetic variation in sexually reproducing organisms.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q122 - Somatic embryogenesis technique in micropropagation

questiontext.text: A technique of micropropagation is

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Micropropagation is the in vitro multiplication of plants under sterile tissue culture conditions to produce large numbers of genetically identical progeny.

Evaluation:
Somatic embryogenesis (formation of bipolar somatic embryos from callus/cell cultures) is a direct, scalable technique of micropropagation used for mass production of plants. Somatic hybridization and protoplast fusion are cell fusion techniques, while embryo rescue is used to save weak hybrid embryos.

Final Conclusion:
Somatic embryogenesis is a technique of micropropagation.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q123 - Translocation as movement of gene between linkage groups

questiontext.text: The movement of a gene from one linkage group to another is called

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
A linkage group represents all genes located linearly on a single chromosome. Transfer of genetic material between non-homologous chromosomes changes the linkage group of the genes.

Evaluation:
The transfer or exchange of a chromosomal segment (and its constituent genes) to a non-homologous chromosome is called translocation. Crossing over occurs between homologous chromosomes (same linkage group), inversion rotates segments within the same chromosome, and duplication repeats a segment on the same chromosome.

Final Conclusion:
The movement of a gene from one linkage group to another is called translocation.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q124 - Multiple alleles at same chromosome locus

questiontext.text: Multiple alleles are present

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Alleles are alternative variant forms of a specific gene. In a population, a gene may exist in more than two allelic forms.

Evaluation:
All multiple alleles of a gene occupy the exact same gene locus on homologous chromosomes across individuals in a population (for example, ABO blood group alleles \(I^A\), \(I^B\), and \(i\)).

Final Conclusion:
Multiple alleles are present at the same locus of the chromosome.

answer.text: at the same locus of the chromosome.
at different loci on the same chromosome.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q125 - Genetic Engineering Approval Committee regulating GM research

questiontext.text: Which body of the Government of India regulates GM research and safety of introducing GM organisms for public services?

generalfeedback.text:
Given Data:
The regulatory framework for biotechnology and bio-safety guidelines in India.

Step-by-Step Evaluation:
The Genetic Engineering Approval Committee (GEAC) is the statutory body set up by the Government of India under the Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change to evaluate the safety, validity, and commercial release of genetically modified (GM) organisms into the environment for public use.

Final Conclusion:
The regulatory body is the Genetic Engineering Approval Committee.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q126 - Activation of Bt protoxin by alkaline gut pH

questiontext.text: In Bt cotton, the Bt toxin present in plant tissue as protoxin is converted into active toxin due to

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Bacillus thuringiensis produces insecticidal crystal (Cry) proteins synthesized as inactive precursors (protoxins).

Evaluation:
When an insect ingests the plant tissue containing inactive Bt protoxin, the alkaline pH of the insect's midgut solubilizes the protein crystals. Midgut proteases then cleave the protoxin, converting it into an active toxin that binds to midgut epithelial cells, creating pores and causing cell lysis.

Final Conclusion:
The protoxin is activated due to the alkaline pH of the insect gut.

answer.text: presence of conversion factors in insect gut.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q127 - Glyphosate tolerant crops resistant to herbicides

questiontext.text: The crops engineered for glyphosate are resistant/tolerant to

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Glyphosate is a broad-spectrum, non-selective systemic herbicide that inhibits the plant enzyme 5-enolpyruvylshikimate-3-phosphate synthase (EPSPS) involved in aromatic amino acid biosynthesis.

Evaluation:
Crops genetically engineered with glyphosate-tolerant genes (such as mutant EPSPS genes) can withstand glyphosate applications, allowing farmers to eliminate surrounding weeds without harming the crop. Therefore, glyphosate-engineered crops are resistant to herbicides.

Final Conclusion:
Crops engineered for glyphosate are resistant/tolerant to herbicides.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q128 - Absence of DNA in ribosomes

questiontext.text: DNA is not present in

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Genetic material (DNA) is localized within the nucleus as well as semi-autonomous organelles (chloroplasts and mitochondria). Ribosomes are non-membrane-bound ribonucleoprotein complexes composed solely of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) and proteins.

Evaluation:
Chloroplasts, mitochondria, and nuclei all possess double-stranded genomic DNA. Ribosomes contain rRNA molecules and proteins, but do not contain DNA.

Final Conclusion:
DNA is not present in ribosomes.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q129 - Fusogens for protoplast fusion

questiontext.text: Which of the following enhances or induces fusion of protoplasts?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Protoplast fusion in somatic hybridization requires chemical fusogens that alter plasma membrane charges to facilitate membrane coalescence.

Evaluation:
Polyethylene glycol (PEG) and high pH / sodium nitrate (\(\text{NaNO}_3\)) treatment are widely recognized fusogenic agents used to induce and enhance protoplast fusion in plant tissue culture. Plant hormones (IAA, kinetin, gibberellins) regulate growth and differentiation rather than plasma membrane fusion.

Final Conclusion:
Polyethylene glycol and sodium nitrate induce the fusion of protoplasts.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q130 - UN climate change conference 2011 venue

questiontext.text: The UN Conference of Parties on climate change in the year 2011 was held in

generalfeedback.text:
Given Data:
International climate change conventions (UNFCCC Conference of the Parties).

Step-by-Step Evaluation:
The 17th United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP 17) took place in Durban, South Africa, from late November to December 2011.

Final Conclusion:
The 2011 UN Conference of Parties was held in South Africa.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q131 - Vertical distribution of species as stratification

questiontext.text: Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels in a biotic community is known as

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Spatial pattern of species arrangements within ecological communities.

Evaluation:
Stratification is the vertical layering of vegetation and organisms in an ecosystem, where different species occupy distinct vertical strata based on height and environmental requirements (e.g., top canopy trees, mid-story shrubs, and ground-layer herbs in a forest ecosystem).

Final Conclusion:
Vertical distribution of different species occupying different levels is known as stratification.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q132 - Matching pairs of in situ and ex situ conservation

questiontext.text: In which of the following, both pairs have correct combination?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Biodiversity conservation strategies are grouped into In situ (on-site protection in natural habitats) and Ex situ (off-site protection outside natural habitats).

Evaluation:
- National parks, wildlife sanctuaries, biosphere reserves, and sacred groves represent In situ conservation.
- Botanical gardens, zoological parks, seed banks, cryopreservation, and tissue culture represent Ex situ conservation.
Matching In situ conservation with National park and Ex situ conservation with Botanical garden provides the correct combination for both pairs.

Final Conclusion:
The correct combination is In situ conservation / National park and Ex situ conservation / Botanical garden.

answer.text:
In situ conservation / National park
Ex situ conservation / Botanical garden

In situ conservation / Cryopreservation
Ex situ conservation / Wildlife sanctuary

In situ conservation / Seed bank
Ex situ conservation / National park

In situ conservation / Tissue culture
Ex situ conservation / Sacred groves

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q133 - Secondary succession in degraded forest

questiontext.text: Secondary succession takes place on/in

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Ecological succession is classified into primary succession (occurring on pristine, previously uncolonized sites devoid of soil) and secondary succession (occurring on sites where existing vegetation was destroyed but soil/organic matter remains).

Evaluation:
Bare rocks, newly created ponds, and newly cooled lava lack pre-existing soil and undergo primary succession. A degraded or burned forest retains soil seed banks and organic substrate, serving as the site for secondary succession.

Final Conclusion:
Secondary succession takes place in a degraded forest.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q134 - Definition of standing crop at trophic level

questiontext.text: The mass of living material at a tropic level at a particular time is called

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Quantitative ecological parameters characterizing trophic levels in an ecosystem.

Evaluation:
Standing crop is defined as the total mass of living organic material (biomass) or number of living organisms present in a specific trophic level at a given point in time. Standing state refers to the amount of non-living inorganic nutrients present in the soil.

Final Conclusion:
The mass of living material at a trophic level at a particular time is called standing crop.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q135 - Rate of organic matter production as GPP

questiontext.text: In an ecosystem, the rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis is termed as

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Ecosystem energetics and primary productivity concepts.

Evaluation:
Gross Primary Productivity (GPP) is the total rate at which organic matter / solar energy is fixed by autotrophic producers through photosynthesis per unit area and time. Net Primary Productivity (NPP) is the rate of storage of organic matter after subtracting producer respiratory losses (\(\text{NPP} = \text{GPP} - R\)).

Final Conclusion:
The rate of production of organic matter during photosynthesis is gross primary productivity.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q136 - Exoskeleton role in insect terrestrial diversification

questiontext.text: Which of the following characteristics is mainly responsible for diversification of insects on land?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Adaptations of arthropods to terrestrial life.

Evaluation:
The tough, waterproof chitinous exoskeleton protects insects against mechanical injury, prevents excessive water loss via desiccation, and provides muscle attachment points. This key adaptation allowed insects to colonize diverse terrestrial niches successfully.

Final Conclusion:
The exoskeleton is mainly responsible for the diversification of insects on land.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q137 - Viviparity in human endoparasite Trichinella spiralis

questiontext.text: Which of the following endoparasites of humans show viviparity?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Reproductive modes among helminthic endoparasites (oviparous versus viviparous/ovoviviparous).

Evaluation:
Trichinella spiralis (the trichina worm) is a viviparous nematode parasite of humans in which adult females release live juvenile larvae directly into the host intestinal mucosa, which then migrate to skeletal muscle. Ascaris, Ancylostoma, and Enterobius lay eggs (oviparous).

Final Conclusion:
The human endoparasite showing viviparity is Trichinella spiralis.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q138 - Class Chondrichthyes features without exception

questiontext.text:
Which of the following represent the correct combination without any exception?

OptionCharacteristicClass
(a)Mammary gland; hair on body; two pairs of limbsMammalia
(b)Mouth ventral; gills without operculum; skin with placoid scales; persistent notochordChondrichthyes
(c)Sucking and circular mouth; jaws absent; integument without scales; paired appendagesCyclostomata
(d)Body covered with feathers; skin moist and glandular; lungs with air sacs; fore limbs from wings;Aves

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Taxonomic characterization of chordate classes and identification of universal diagnostic traits.

Evaluation:
- Mammalia: Whales/dolphins lack body hair and have modified flippers instead of typical limbs; egg-laying mammals exist.
- Cyclostomata: Lack paired appendages (they have unpaired fins).
- Aves: Birds possess dry skin devoid of glands except for the preen/oil gland at the tail base.
- Chondrichthyes: All cartilaginous fishes possess a ventral mouth, separate gill slits without an operculum, tough skin with placoid scales, and a persistent notochord.

Final Conclusion:
The combination representing Class Chondrichthyes features without exception is Mouth ventral; gills without operculum; skin with placoid scales; persistent notochord.

Mammary gland; hair on body; two pairs of limbs — Mammalia

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q139 - Oviparous mammal Platypus

questiontext.text: Which of the following animals is not viviparous?

generalfeedback.text:
Conceptual Principle:
Reproductive patterns in Mammalia (viviparous Eutherians/Metatherians versus oviparous Prototherians).

Evaluation:
Flying fox (bat), elephant, and whale are viviparous placental mammals that give birth to live young. Platypus (*Ornithorhynchus*) is a primitive egg-laying (oviparous) mammal belonging to subclass Prototheria (monotremes).

Final Conclusion:
The animal that is not viviparous is Platypus.

name.text: NEET_UG_BIOLOGY_2015_MCQ_Q140 - Erythropoiesis site in red bone marrow

questiontext.text: Erythropoiesis starts in

generalfeedback.text:
